content: Cordlife Ltd. is a company specializing in cord blood banking, headquartered in Singapore and publicly listed on the Australian Stock Exchange. The organization operates three cord blood processing and storage facilities located in Singapore, Hong Kong, Jakarta (Indonesia), and Sydney (Australia). The company was established in May 2001, becoming one of the first private cord blood banks in Southeast Asia and the first of its kind in Singapore. In December 2002, Cordlife facilitated the first cord blood transplant in Singapore using a privately banked source. In April 2003, the company acquired Cytomatrix LLC, a biotechnology firm based in Massachusetts, USA. Subsequently, Cordlife expanded its operations across Southeast Asia and North Asia, inaugurating a facility in Hong Kong in March 2005. In September 2005, the Singapore facility achieved accreditation from the American Association of Blood Banks (AABB), making it the only private cord blood bank in the region to hold this distinction. In November 2005, Cordlife entered the Australian market by acquiring a majority stake in BioCell Pty Ltd. By January 2006, the company had established a presence in Kolkata, India, with the launch event attended by Singapore’s Senior Minister Goh Chok Tong. In September 2006, Cordlife announced plans to open a facility in Jakarta, Indonesia, which officially commenced operations in September 2007. The Kolkata facility was projected to open by the end of 2007. Additionally, the company expressed intentions to construct a larger facility in Singapore. In December 2006, Cordlife was recognized as a Technology Pioneer 2007 by the World Economic Forum. In March 2007, the company rebranded itself as Cordlife Ltd. to emphasize its core focus on cord blood banking.
